title: E2E latency fuzz harness and regression logbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working log for the E2E latency fuzzing harness: a lightweight orchestration layer that generates realistic, adversarial traffic across model variants, scheduler configs, and KV cache states to (1) surface regressions in median/p95 latency, (2) exercise kernel code paths that are rarely hit by unit microbenchmarks, and (3) produce trace artifacts usable by the microtrace replay pipeline. The goal is a repeatable CI gating job + periodic nightlies for broader coverage.

Why we need this (short):
- Microbenchmarks and kernel unit tests catch correctness and tight inner-loop performance, but they miss cross-cutting interactions: scheduler queuing, golden-path prefix cache hits + eviction storms, and fallback routing behavior.
- Past incidents showed regressions that only manifested under moderate heterogenous load with KV cache churn and occasional long-context requests.
- Intend to reduce time-to-detect regressions and give SRE/eng reproducible traces for postmortem.

High-level design:
- Harness driver (python glue) that coordinates: request generator, workload profiler, runtime config applier, tracer collector.
- Workload templates: metadata-driven YAML describing model (arch/seq-len), prompt mix (ratio short/medium/long), parallelism, inter-arrival distribution, and KV cache pre-population/eviction patterns.
- Config permutations: scheduler policies (priority vs FIFO vs LIFO-before-batch), kernel selection hinting (fp16 vs int8 paths), and KV cache sizing/eviction-policy toggles.
- Observability outputs: request-level traces (open-telemetry spans), aggregated microbench metrics (per-kernel compute time, queueing time, key-value store ops), and a compressed artifact bundle for replay.

Key components and responsibilities:
- request-generator.py: produce realistic text/chat requests with parameterized token lengths and function-calling patterns. Supports scriptable burst/fuzz phases.
- config-applier: uses runtime control plane API to set scheduler knobs and kernel hints per test iteration. Reverts to baseline after run.
- kv-populator: preloads KV cache with synthetic prefixes + blackbox TTL setters to simulate warm and cold scenarios. Has two modes: steady-state and eviction-storm.
- tracer-collector: aggregates OTLP spans to a local minio bucket and optionally forwards to the microtrace replay harness.
- validator: lightweight smoke checks post-run to ensure outputs are syntactically valid and no runtime exceptions occurred.

Test matrix (examples):
- Short burst, no KV cache: 200 qps for 30s, model=redwood-v1-small, scheduler=fifo. Expect p99 < 120ms.
- Steady medium load with cold cache: 50 qps for 5m, kv-mode=eviction-storm, kernel-hint=int8. Monitor increase in median and kv-op latencies.
- Heterogeneous mix: 20% long-context (2k tokens), 60% medium, 20% short; schedule=priority; ensure KV cache hit ratio stays > 0.6.
- Kernel stress: force rarer kernel code paths by crafting specific model shapes and sequence lengths; collect per-kernel op timings.

Regression detection and triage flow:
- Define baseline artifacts per branch: nightly baseline bundles stored under s3://redwood-ci/e2e-baselines/{branch}/{date}. Baseline includes traces + aggregated metrics.
- Regression detector compares current run to baseline with heuristics and thresholds: median change > 15% and p95 change > 20% or absolute increase > 50ms flags an incident.
- On flag, harness crates an issue skeleton: summary, reproducible seed, configs, link to trace bundle, and top-N offending kernel and scheduler metrics. File auto-assigns to oncall rotation and eng-owner suggested from blame mapping.

Trace shaping and replay considerations:
- Each run produces a run-id tag and deterministic seed when possible. Request generator writes the exact prompt bodies and sequence info so replay can rehydrate KV cache state and request ordering.
- To handle non-deterministic kernels (floating point noise, async scheduling), replay harness must accept a tolerance mask for numerical assertions and focus on timeline reproduction and span-level ordering.

Known gotchas and past lessons learned (from incidents and experiments):
- Eviction storms: rapid KV cache evictions produce long tail latency spikes due to synchronous eviction callbacks holding the scheduler thread. Mitigation: convert eviction callbacks to async worker; in the meantime, add fuzz phase that triggers eviction patterns.
- Kernel fallback loop: scheduler policy that aggressively reassigns failing requests caused repeated kernel init calls and a cascading slowdown. Fix in runtime required but harness should detect repeated kernel init events in traces.
- Batcher starvation: very small long-context workload mixed with many short requests can cause the batching window to shrink and increase per-token overhead. Add template to simulate this mix.

Implementation notes and short-term plan (next 8 weeks):
- Week 0-1: carve out python harness repo module and basic driver + one workload template covering baseline smoke test. (owner: Benji)
- Week 2: kv-populator + steady-state mode implemented; integrate with runtime control plane API for cache sizing. (owner: Claire)
- Week 3: tracer collection + upload to nightly bucket; wire up baseline storage. (owner: Aisha)
- Week 4-5: regression detector prototype and issue auto-creation; add kernel/op level counters to runtime traces. (owner: Diego)
- Week 6-8: CI integration (gating check on PRs that touch scheduler/kernels), nightly expanded matrix, runbook for triage.

Automation and CI gating ideas:
- Lightweight smoke as pre-merge: single-template run with deterministic seed and small duration. Failure blocks PR.
- Full e2e is expensive; schedule large matrix as nightly job and weekly expanded runs. Alerting to channel with auto-linked issue on regression.

What to log in the artifact bundle:
- run-metadata.json (deterministic fields only): run id, seed, config, timestamps
- prompts.jsonl (full request list)
- otel-spans.{ndjson,traceproto} compressed
- aggregated-metrics.csv with per-kernel timings and queueing breakdown
- diff-report.txt summarizing top deltas vs baseline

Open design questions (for the team):
- CI gating threshold: how conservative should pre-merge checks be to avoid noise? Suggest: strict for any PR touching scheduler or kernel selection code, permissive elsewhere.
- Where to store long-term baselines and how to version them with branch lifecycles? Proposed s3 with manifest referencing commit SHAs.
- How much of the payload generation should live in the harness versus being synthetic templates embedded into the runtime testbench?

Immediate actions (TODOS):
- [ ] Create initial harness repo skeleton and add README (Benji)
- [ ] Add runtime API contract doc for config-applier (Claire)
- [ ] Draft issue auto-creation template and add to triage-runbook (Aisha)
- [ ] Add a kernel metric tag in runtime traces (Diego)

Appendix: quick debugging checklist for a flagged run
- Confirm run-id and baseline used in diff-report.
- Check KV op histogram: sudden spike indicates eviction or remote store pressure.
- Inspect kernel-init spans: frequency and wall-time.
- Look for queuing spikes aligned to GC/compaction markers in infra metrics.
- Re-run with reduced matrix to isolate variable (turn off eviction-storm, switch scheduler to fifo, toggle kernel hint).

Notes-to-self and scribbles:
- consider adding a mode that fuzzes model shapes across the small-model family to force fallback to different kernel paths.
- add a lightweight prometheus exporter in harness for quick live dashboards during runs.
- think about shipping a small dashboard in console under "ci/e2e-fuzz" showing last 7 days of run deltas.

Contact / owners: Aisha (aisha@redwood.ai) primary owner for rollout; Benji and Claire for implementation; Diego for trace/runtime hook changes.

End of logbook entry (working doc).
